a deep learning based fingerprint spoof detection approach that leverages minutiae-based local patch features can achieve state of the art accuracy for fingerprint spoof attacks.

the proposed method achieves state-of-the-art performance in fingerprint spoof detection under a variety of testing scenarios, such as intra-sensor, inter-sensor, cross material, cross-dataset, and cross-sensor testing.
we propose a deep learning based approach to fingerprint spoof detection that achieves state of the art performance on public domain LivDet datasets.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a spoof detection algorithm which is accurate, generalizable, and can be easily deployed on mobile devices.
the development of spoof detection methods that can generalize well across different datasets and testing conditions.
developing generalizable spoof detection methods that are not limited by a particular sensor, spoof material, or dataset.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed approach achieves state of the art performance on fingerprint spoof detection for all the testing scenarios.
the proposed approach is a state of the art fingerprint spoof detection algorithm.
the proposed approach is the first and the only method in the literature that provides a state of the art accuracy in fingerprint spoof detection across all three publicly available LivDet datasets.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
our proposed algorithm achieves the state-of-the-art performance in fingerprint spoof detection across multiple testing scenarios.
we have developed an accurate, robust, and generalizable approach for detecting spoof attacks against fingerprint recognition systems.

our approach is the best performing algorithm for fingerprint spoof detection on the LivDet 2011, 13 and 15 datasets, and the proposed approach is also the first to report cross-sensor and cross-dataset testing results on the LivDet datasets.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed approach, which does not require training data for spoof materials, provides a generalizable solution for spoof detection that works well for different types of spoof materials.

the proposed deep learning approach can be used for fingerprint spoof detection with high accuracy, even when training and testing are performed under different sensor, material, and dataset conditions.
local minutia-based patches can be used to develop generalizable and accurate fingerprint spoof detectors.
